groups.label: The guide's quick checks
groups.note: The three numbers Chalkbeat and The City Reporter suggest looking at first.

groups.label: Learning
groups.note: Test proficiency tracks a school's demographics closely. DOE's impact score compares students with similar students elsewhere, which is the fairer read on what the school adds.

groups.label: Teachers and resources
groups.note: More money per student doesn't always mean more resources: small schools that are losing students can look flush under the city's hold-harmless budget rules.

groups.label: Special education
groups.note: DOE counts a student as served if the services started at some point in the year, which can hide delays.

metrics.label: Teachers who say the principal runs the school well
metrics.def: Share of responding teachers who agree or strongly agree: "The principal/program leader at this school is an effective manager who makes the school run smoothly." (Teacher survey q29; part of the Teacher-Principal Trust measure.)

metrics.label: Teachers who would recommend the school to families
metrics.def: Share of responding teachers who agree or strongly agree: "I would recommend this school to parents/guardians seeking a place for their child." (Teacher survey q22; School Commitment measure.)

metrics.label: Students chronically absent (missed 10% or more of days)
metrics.def: Share of students with attendance of 90 percent or less (absent 10 percent or more of their days). Students must be enrolled at least 10 days and present at least 1 day to be counted.

metrics.label: DOE impact score: progress against similar students
metrics.def: DOE's value-added score: the school's results minus what the same students would be expected to achieve at an average city school, given incoming test scores, poverty, disability and English learner status. Standardized within school type; 0.50 is the median.

metrics.label: DOE performance score: results against all schools of its type
metrics.def: DOE's score for raw results (test scores, or graduation and college readiness for high schools), standardized within school type; 0.50 is the median. It doesn't adjust for who the students are.

metrics.label: Students proficient in English (state test, grades 3-8)
metrics.def: Share of students tested in grades 3-8 who scored at Level 3 or 4 on the state English test. District schools: spring 2026, from DOE. Charter schools: spring 2025, from NYSED, whose 2026 school file is not out yet.
metrics.source: New York State tests (DOE results; NYSED for charter schools)

metrics.label: Students proficient in math (state test, grades 3-8)
metrics.def: Share of students tested in grades 3-8 who scored at Level 3 or 4 on the state math test. Eighth graders who took the Algebra I Regents instead are not counted, so at some middle schools this describes only part of the grade. District schools: spring 2026, from DOE. Charter schools: spring 2025, from NYSED.
metrics.source: New York State tests (DOE results; NYSED for charter schools)

metrics.label: Four-year graduation rate
metrics.def: Share of the Cohort 2021 (students who first entered 9th grade in 2021-22) who earned a Local or Regents diploma within four years, including August graduates.

metrics.label: College and career readiness score (0-100)
metrics.def: Average College and Career Readiness (CCR) score of students in the school's four-year cohort (Class of 2025) after their fourth year. Each student scores 0-100 based on course grades, test scores, advanced courses and endorsements. This is an average score, not the percent of students who are ready.

metrics.label: Students taking an advanced course (AP, IB, college credit)
metrics.def: Share of students enrolled, as of Oct. 31, 2024, in at least one credit-bearing advanced course: AP, IB, CLEP, a college-credit course, a DOE-certified college preparatory (CPCC) course, or other advanced math/science (Algebra II, Calculus, Chemistry, Physics). The guide does not state the denominator; for 02M475 the Snapshot shows "2776 (85%)" against 3,266 enrolled, i.e. school enrollment.

metrics.label: Students who passed an industry-recognized technical (CTE) exam
metrics.def: % Passing an Industry-Recognized Technical Assessment (the CTE certification exam measure); base is the four-year cohort (same N as the CCPCI).

metrics.label: Students who feel safe in the hallways and cafeteria
metrics.def: Share of responding students (grades 6-12) answering Safe or Very Safe to "Do you feel safe in the hallways and the cafeteria?" (Student survey q40; Safety measure.)

metrics.label: Students who say most or all teachers support them when upset
metrics.def: Share of responding students answering Most or All of their teachers to "How many of your teachers do you feel support you when you are upset?" (Student survey q13; Student-Teacher Trust measure.)

metrics.label: Students with a trusted adult at school
metrics.def: Share of responding students answering Often or Very often to "How often do you feel like there is at least one trusted adult at this school you could talk to if you needed to?" (Student survey q34; Social-Emotional measure.)

metrics.label: Students who say classmates vape often
metrics.def: Share of responding students answering Very often or Often to "How often do students in this school vape?" This is the unfavorable side of the item; DOE's percent favorable is the remainder (Sometimes/Never). New in 2026, reported under Additional Questions and not scored in any measure.

metrics.label: Families satisfied with their child's education
metrics.def: Share of responding K-12 families answering Satisfied or Very satisfied to "How satisfied are you with the following? The education my child has received this year." (Family survey q36; Family Satisfaction with Child's Education measure.)

metrics.label: Average daily attendance
metrics.def: Total days present divided by total days on register for all students at the school over the school year (all grades, including Pre-K where offered).

metrics.label: Suspensions per 100 students
metrics.def: Principal's and superintendent's suspensions in 2024-25 per 100 students enrolled. DOE redacts counts of 1 to 5, so schools with few suspensions often have no figure. Neither high nor low is good on its own: a high rate can mean strict discipline, and a low one doesn't guarantee a calm school.
metrics.source: DOE Local Law 93 discipline report; enrollment from DOE Demographic Snapshot

metrics.label: Teachers with three or more years of experience
metrics.def: Percent of teachers with 3 or more years of experience (DOE column label; the 2024-25 Educator Guides give no further definition).

metrics.label: Average class size
metrics.def: Average number of students per class across the school's general education, ICT, G&T and accelerated classes (K-5 official classes plus every 6-12 course section, all subjects), as of 6/15/26. Self-contained special classes are left out, as in DOE's own 'overall' averages. Computed by this script as total students / total classes over those rows; the same formula on the whole file reproduces DOE's citywide 23.5.

metrics.label: Classes within the state's class-size cap
metrics.def: Share of the school's non-exempt classes at or below the state class-size caps (K-3: 20, grades 4-8: 23, grades 9-12: 25, 6-12 PE and performing groups: 40), as of 10/31/25. DOE's definition: 'the total number of non-exempt classes at or below the cap out of the total number of non-exempt classes.' Excludes self-contained classes, District 75/79/88 schools and charters. Computed by summing Table C's K-5 grade rows and 6-12 course rows for the school; the same sum citywide gives DOE's 64%.

metrics.label: Students per guidance counselor
metrics.def: DOE's ratio of 2024-25 enrollment to guidance counselors (Total GC). Kept only where the school has at least 1 counselor. Below that, DOE's file divides by 1 instead of the real count, so the ratio is stored as null. Citywide DOE reports 1:259 for all schools and 1:182 for schools with high school grades. A commonly cited benchmark is 250 students per counselor, fewer in high-needs schools.

metrics.label: Spending per student
metrics.def: Per pupil expenditures using federal and state/local funds (FED_STATE_LOCAL_EXP / PUPIL_COUNT_TOT): the school's total non-excluded expenditures divided by its enrollment.

metrics.label: PTA money raised per student
metrics.def: Derived: Total Income divided by the school's 2024-25 Total Enrollment as given in the same workbook.

metrics.label: Students enrolled
metrics.def: Students on the Oct. 31 audited register (BEDS day for charters).

metrics.label: Enrollment change since 2021-22
metrics.def: Change in enrollment from 2021-22 to 2025-26. A drop can reflect a shrinking neighborhood, not the school.

metrics.label: Building use: enrollment as a share of capacity
metrics.def: Calculated by dividing org. enrollment by org. capacity (target calculation). 1.00 = exactly full.

metrics.label: Economic need index
metrics.def: DOE's estimate of the share of students facing economic hardship (public assistance, temporary housing, recent immigration or a high-poverty census tract).

metrics.label: Students with disabilities
metrics.def: Students with an IEP as of June 2026.

metrics.label: English language learners
metrics.def: Students identified as English language learners.

metrics.label: Students with IEPs fully receiving their special-ed programs
metrics.def: Of students with IEPs as of June 2025 whose IEP recommends a special education program (Special Class, Integrated Co-Teaching or SETSS), the share "fully receiving": DOE counts a student as fully receiving "if there is an exact match between the IEP and the course enrollment in the STARS scheduling system." (2024-25 EMS Educator Guide.)

metrics.label: Students with IEPs fully receiving related services (speech, OT, counseling)
metrics.def: Of students with IEPs whose IEP recommends related services (speech, occupational or physical therapy, counseling and the like), the share whose received services "match all of the recommended services." (2024-25 EMS Educator Guide.)

metrics.label: Average co-taught (ICT) class
metrics.def: Average students per Integrated Co-Teaching class (a general and a special education teacher together), K-5 official classes plus all 6-12 course sections, as of 6/15/26. Following DOE, combined ICT & G&T and ICT & accelerated classes count as ICT. Computed as total students / total classes.

metrics.label: Average self-contained special class
metrics.def: Average students per self-contained special education class (K-5/K-8 settings 12:1:1, 12:1, 8:1:1, 6:1:1, 15:1, 12:1:4, plus 6-12 'SC' course sections), as of 6/15/26. These sizes are set by students' IEP settings and are not covered by the state caps. Null means the school reported no self-contained classes. Computed as total students / total classes.

metrics.label: Building accessibility
metrics.def: DOE's accessibility description for the school's main building: 'Fully Accessible' or 'Partially Accessible'. Null when the main building isn't on DOE's list. DOE: 'Non-accessible buildings are not included on the BAP List.'
